title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space (Word2Vec)
inputs: A large text corpus (sequence of words/tokens)
outputs: Continuous vector representations (embeddings) for each word in the vocabulary
pseudocode:
1. Load and preprocess text corpus
2. Build vocabulary (words occurring >= min_count times)
3. Initialize word vectors randomly (vocab_size × embedding_dim)
4. For each epoch:
5.   For each word w in corpus:
6.     CBOW variant:
7.       context = words within window_size of w
8.       context_vec = mean(vectors[context])
9.       Predict w from context_vec (hierarchical softmax or negative sampling)
10.      Update context_vec and w vector via gradient descent
11.    Skip-gram variant:
12.      For each context word c within window_size of w:
13.        Predict c from w vector (hierarchical softmax or negative sampling)
14.        Update w and c vectors via gradient descent
15.  Optionally decay learning_rate
16. Return learned word vectors
key_equations: CBOW objective: maximize log p(w_t | w_{t-c}, ..., w_{t-1}, w_{t+1}, ..., w_{t+c})
Skip-gram objective: maximize (1/T) Σ_t Σ_{-c≤j≤c, j≠0} log p(w_{t+j} | w_t)
Negative sampling: log σ(v'_{w_O}^T v_{w_I}) + Σ_{i=1}^k E_{w_i~P_n(w)} [log σ(-v'_{w_i}^T v_{w_I})]
Hierarchical softmax: p(w|context) = Π_{j=1}^{L(w)-1} σ([n(w,j+1)=ch(n(w,j))] · v'_{n(w,j)}^T v_context)
evaluation_dataset: Google News corpus (6B tokens), Semantic-Syntactic Word Relationship test set (8869 semantic + 10675 syntactic questions), Microsoft Sentence Completion Challenge
toy_dataset_suggestion: text8 dataset (first 100M characters of Wikipedia, ~17M tokens) or a small subset (first 10M tokens). Alternatively, a synthetic text corpus or the Brown corpus from NLTK.
key_figure_description: A table or bar chart showing accuracy on the Semantic-Syntactic Word Relationship test versus model architecture (RNNLM, NNLM, CBOW, Skip-gram) for fixed embedding dimension (e.g., 300) and training data size. X-axis: model type; Y-axis: accuracy percentage on semantic questions, syntactic questions, and overall. Expect Skip-gram to excel on semantic, CBOW on syntactic.
notes: For a toy implementation: (1) Use negative sampling instead of hierarchical softmax for simplicity. (2) Train on a small corpus (text8 subset) for 1-3 epochs. (3) Evaluate on a subset of the word analogy questions (e.g., capital-common-countries, past-tense). (4) Focus on either CBOW or Skip-gram, not both. (5) Skip distributed training and parallelization. (6) The key trend to reproduce: Skip-gram captures semantic relationships (e.g., king-man+woman≈queen) measurably better than simpler baselines, observable even in toy setting with cosine similarity tests.
